docstring:
Does there exist, for all $r\geq 2$, a basis $A$ of order $r$ (so that $f_r(n)>0$ for all
large $n$) such that $$\sum_{n\leq x}f_r(n)^2 \ll x$$ for all $x$?
references: [Ru90] Ruzsa, Imre Z., A just basis. Monatsh. Math. (1990), 145--151.
[Er80] Erdős, Paul, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory. Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), 89--115.
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ r ≥ 2,
    ∃ A,
      (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos1192.f_r A r n > 0) ∧
        (fun x => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (x + 1), ↑(Erdos1192.f_r A r n) ^ 2) =O[Filter.atTop] fun x => ↑x
